body.statement: For every compact \(K\subset(0,\infty)^3\), there are \(C_K<\infty\) and \(n_K\) such that, for every \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in K\), every \(n\geq n_K\) with \(G_n=1\), and the estimator \(\widehat{\tau}^{G}_n(x_0)\) derived from \(\mathfrak H_G\), \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{band}}}\mathbb{E}_P\left|\widehat{\tau}^{G}_n(x_0)-\tau_P(x_0)\right|\leq C_K\left[(h_n^*)^\gamma+\left\{\frac{h_n^*}{(k_n^*)^{1/d}}\right\}^{\alpha+\beta}+\left(\frac{1}{N_n^*}\left\{1+\frac{k_n^*}{N_n^*}\right\}\right)^{1/2}\right]=C_K r_n^*.\] The estimator is an everywhere-defined same-sample M\"obius-stabilized empirical-Gram local HOIF and uses no estimate or smoothness condition for \(f_P\). On the explicitly restricted class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{band}}\), the construction therefore attains the KBRW three-term objective on the \(G_n\) branch without the density-estimation or density-ratio condition used in KBRW Theorem 2. No inclusion relation between the two theorem classes is asserted.
body.justification: It localizes same-sample stabilization at the random effective size \(N_n^*\) and, on the explicitly restricted fixed positive-band class, avoids a density-estimation remainder without a logarithmic risk loss.
body.gap: Liu et al. prove stabilization for global bilinear forms with deterministic sample size, while the KBRW upper theorem uses a local covariate-law condition; neither result supplies density-free control of weighted occupancy, leverage, and collisions in the same local sample under the fixed positive-band restriction.
body.consumer: It supplies density-free optimal pointwise CATE estimation whenever the optimizer-selected local rank is empirically feasible.
